overview.title: What is Eleutheria?
overview.text: Eleutheria is a new nation project seeking a sovereign territory in the South Pacific built on limited government, free markets, and personal liberty.

overview.title: Who joins Eleutheria?
overview.text: Eleutheria attracts liberty-minded individuals, entrepreneurs, and investors interested in the free private city and new nation movement. Virtual citizenship is open to anyone who supports the core values of limited government, free markets, and the non-aggression principle. A dedicated Christian stream, Nova Nicaea, welcomes members who want to build intentional faith-based communities within the new nation.

overview.title: Eleutheria's Two Proposed Territories
overview.text: The Pacifica project proposes to develop a free city on Funafuti Atoll in Tuvalu under a 99-year sovereign lease, creating 3.6 square kilometers of raised land through reclamation. A second proposal, Meliora, targets the Carteret Islands atoll in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, aiming to bring sustainable development to one of the Pacific's most climate-vulnerable regions.

history.text:
Eleutheria began in 2019 as the New Nation Project, inspired by Bir Tawil - one of Earth's last unclaimed territories - as a potential site for a liberty-focused polity. When conflict in Sudan made the Bir Tawil region inaccessible, the organization pivoted to pursue sovereign lease arrangements with existing Pacific island nations.

The project adopted the name Eleutheria - the Greek term for liberty - following a vote at its third Parliament meeting in August 2024. On August 6, 2024, the founding constitution was ratified by citizen referendum and the organization formally incorporated as the Confederation of Eleutheria Association Inc., a non-profit in Victoria, Australia. Co-founders Steve Clancy, Jonathan Weinert, and Eric Belarbre lead the organization alongside a committee that includes Carly Jackson, Operations Manager at [The Seasteading Institute](https://www.seasteading.org/eleutheria-podcast/).

By 2024, Eleutheria had developed two concurrent proposals - Pacifica in Tuvalu and Meliora in Bougainville - and secured $7M in indicative land option commitments. Market research showed 90% support among surveyed Tuvaluans for the Pacifica proposal. In May 2025, Eleutheria was recognized as a business member of The Seasteading Institute. The organization held its annual general meeting in November 2025.

location:
Eleutheria has two proposed territories in the South Pacific; neither has begun physical development as of 2026.

Pacifica is planned for the western side of Funafuti Atoll in Tuvalu, a South Pacific island nation of about 12,000 people located roughly 4,000 kilometers northeast of Australia. The proposal involves reclaiming 8 kilometers of land on the atoll to create 3.6 square kilometers of raised land above current sea levels, providing a stable foundation for housing, seasteads, and infrastructure. The city would operate under a 99-year renewable sovereign lease from the Tuvaluan government; if not renewed, all reclaimed land reverts to Tuvalu. The [Why Tuvalu](https://www.newnationproject.org/why-tuvalu) page details the climate and governance rationale.

Meliora is proposed for the south-west of the Carteret Islands atoll in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Papua New Guinea. The Carteret Islands are among the Pacific's most climate-vulnerable low-lying territories, and Meliora aims to deliver investment, infrastructure, and sustainable livelihoods to the region.

Eleutheria does not yet have formal government recognition or approval of either proposal.
duration:
Eleutheria is designed as a permanent settlement for full-time residents once a territory is operational. There are no fixed program terms or rotating cohorts - residency would be long-term, comparable to living in any small city or nation.

During the current pre-territorial phase, participation is entirely remote. Virtual citizens join online, vote in Parliamentary elections held on a two-year cycle, and engage with the growing community while the organization negotiates its sovereign lease.
pricing:
Virtual citizenship is free. Applying for citizenship costs nothing and includes the right to claim a future land parcel at no additional charge once a territory is established.

The [Tuvalu Pioneers](https://www.newnationproject.org/fundraising/p/tuvalu-pioneers) program offers a $110 donation tier. Contributors receive a 1 sqm land parcel voucher for the proposed Pacifica city, plus 1 sqm vested to Tuvalu's sovereign wealth fund if the Pacifica proposal succeeds. This is a conditional pledge contingent on securing the sovereign lease, not a guarantee of land title.

Larger investment opportunities are available via the [investment waitlist](https://www.newnationproject.org/waitlist) as Eleutheria raises capital for sovereign lease and development costs.

howToEnter.text:
Applying for virtual citizenship in Eleutheria is free and open to anyone who supports the project's core values. Applicants choose between two registration pathways: Unaligned Registration (for those who affirm limited government, free markets, and the non-aggression principle) or [Nova Nicaea Registration](https://www.newnationproject.org/nova-nicaea) (for Christians who affirm the Nicene Creed and are baptized).

Physical residency is not yet available - Eleutheria has not secured its sovereign lease as of 2026. Virtual citizens participate in online Parliamentary elections and can claim a future land parcel at no cost. Supporters interested in early investment can join the [investment waitlist](https://www.newnationproject.org/waitlist).

faqs.question: What is Eleutheria and what is it trying to build?
faqs.answer: Eleutheria is a new nation project working toward a sovereign city in the South Pacific. The primary plan is to secure a 99-year sovereign lease from Tuvalu to build Pacifica, a free private city on reclaimed land at Funafuti Atoll combining land development with seasteading technology. A second territory, Meliora, is proposed for the Carteret Islands in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea.

faqs.question: Where will Eleutheria be located?
faqs.answer: Eleutheria has two proposed territories. Pacifica is planned for Funafuti Atoll in Tuvalu. Meliora is proposed for the Carteret Islands atoll in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea. Neither site has begun physical development as of 2026, and Eleutheria does not yet have formal government approval for either proposal.

faqs.question: Is virtual citizenship in Eleutheria free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Applying for virtual citizenship is free of charge and includes a future land parcel claim at no cost. The [Tuvalu Pioneers](https://www.newnationproject.org/fundraising/p/tuvalu-pioneers) program offers an optional $110 donation tier for a 1 sqm land voucher. [Apply here](https://www.newnationproject.org/apply) to get started.

faqs.question: What are Eleutheria's core principles?
faqs.answer: Eleutheria is built on four pillars: limited government (minimizing state intrusion into economic and social life), free markets, the non-aggression principle (the ethical stance that initiating force is wrong), and Judeo-Christian values. The project separates church and state, welcoming residents of all faiths while allowing free worship.

faqs.question: Who founded Eleutheria?
faqs.answer: Eleutheria was co-founded by Steve Clancy (Melbourne, insurance broker, President and Secretary), Jonathan Weinert (Germany, finance specialist and published author on governance), and Eric Belarbre (Sydney, engineer specializing in decentralized systems). Committee members include Kristin Silitonga (Treasurer), Carly Jackson (Operations Manager at The Seasteading Institute), and Andy Starr (nation-building project designer).

faqs.question: What is the Pacifica project?
faqs.answer: Pacifica is Eleutheria's proposed free private city on Funafuti Atoll in Tuvalu. The plan involves reclaiming 8 kilometers of land to create 3.6 square kilometers of raised land under a 99-year sovereign lease. The city would use OTEC renewable energy and tokenize property as blockchain-based Real World Assets. Market research indicates 90% support among surveyed Tuvaluans. [Learn more about Pacifica](https://www.newnationproject.org/pacifica).

faqs.question: What is the Meliora project in Bougainville?
faqs.answer: Meliora is Eleutheria's second proposed territory, planned for the south-west of the Carteret Islands atoll in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Papua New Guinea. The Carteret Islands are among the Pacific's most climate-vulnerable low-lying areas. Meliora aims to bring sustainable infrastructure, investment, and livelihood opportunities to the region.

faqs.question: What is Nova Nicaea?
faqs.answer: Nova Nicaea is a Christian membership stream within the New Nation Project. It seeks to establish intentional Christian communities within Eleutheria's free cities. Members affirm the Nicene Creed and are baptized. Virtual citizenship in Nova Nicaea is free and includes prayer support and community access. [Learn more about Nova Nicaea](https://www.newnationproject.org/nova-nicaea).

faqs.question: When will Eleutheria have physical territory?
faqs.answer: As of 2026, Eleutheria does not have formal government recognition or approval of either the Pacifica or Meliora proposals. The organization is actively negotiating a sovereign lease with Tuvalu and has secured $7M in indicative land option commitments. No construction timeline has been formally announced. Join the [waitlist](https://www.newnationproject.org/waitlist) to be notified of progress.

faqs.question: How is Eleutheria governed?
faqs.answer: Eleutheria operates under a constitution ratified on August 6, 2024. Governance includes a Parliament (House of Representatives) of 2-100 members elected to 2-year terms, an executive branch of Commissioners appointed for 4-year terms who cannot legislate, and an independent judiciary with jury trials for all criminal matters. Virtual citizens vote in online elections. The most recent annual general meeting was held in November 2025.
